children.name: Agentic Drafting and Multi-Model Workflows
children.blurb: Agentic drafting and multi-model workflows cover the use of AI systems that can plan, draft, revise, and route narrative tasks across more than one language model.

children.name: Outlining and Plot Structure
children.blurb: Outlining and plot structure covers the systematic planning of narrative arcs, beats, scenes, and character trajectories before drafting, and the structural templates that shape a story.

children.name: Character Voice and Dialogue
children.blurb: Character voice and dialogue in AI covers the modeling, generation, and editing of a character's distinct speech patterns, including word choice, rhythm, idiom, and conversational habits.

children.name: World-Building and Continuity
children.blurb: This page covers the use of AI to create, organize, and check the internal consistency of fictional worlds across novels, serial fiction, games, and screenwriting.

children.name: Developmental Editing
children.blurb: Developmental editing is the structural work on a manuscript or narrative: shaping plot, character arcs, pacing, point of view, theme, and overall architecture before line editing or copyediting.

sections.body: This field covers the use of AI systems to draft prose, build outlines, write dialogue, track continuity, and perform developmental editing. In practice, writers use large language models to generate scene drafts from prompts, to propose plot beats, and to rewrite passages in a chosen voice. Some tools maintain a story bible or character sheet and flag when a new draft contradicts earlier details. Developmental editing systems now summarize a manuscript's structure, point out pacing problems, and suggest where a subplot could be strengthened. These are not autonomous novelists, they are assistants that produce text and notes a human author must review and revise.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Drafting and dialogue generation are reliable for short passages but often drift in tone or logic over a long manuscript. Outlining tools can produce competent three-act or five-act structures, yet they tend to recycle familiar patterns and struggle with genuinely surprising turns. Continuity tracking works well for simple facts like eye color or a character's hometown, but it fails on implied relationships, emotional consistency, and thematic echoes. Developmental editing is the least solved area, current systems can identify obvious repetition and plot holes, but they cannot judge whether a scene earns its emotional payoff or whether a metaphor is fresh. The honest limit is that these tools reduce some mechanical labor, they do not replace judgment, taste, or lived experience.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how multiple models are chained together to produce longer drafts should start with Agentic Drafting and Multi-Model Workflows, which explains the practical setup of using one model for prose and another for critique. Outlining and Plot Structure covers the templates and prompting methods that turn a premise into a scene list, and it is the best page for someone who has a story idea but no plan. Character Voice and Dialogue focuses on keeping a character's speech consistent across scenes, including the use of style guides and few-shot examples. World-Building and Continuity is where the site explains how a story bible is maintained and how contradictions are caught, useful for serial fiction or long series. Developmental Editing rounds out the section by describing how AI reads a full draft and returns structural notes, which is the page for writers who already have a complete manuscript and want a second pass.
